description:
From: Bugs and Cleanup. User-approved 2026-11-25 ("Land, ticket overload choice").

Evidence: lib declares two specs for concat, `@spec concat([a], [b]) :: [a | b]` and `@spec concat([a], b) :: maybe_improper_list(a, b) | b`. fz gives every call the union of both results instead of the result of the overload its argument types select. So `list ++ list` loses its proper-list result. After fz-sc8.22.3 (#903), the distiller's ++ sites pay for this: largest drive +412, derivations +219, reads +2,732. Measured in sc8.22.3's probes (B&C scratchpad s22/b3/table*.txt).

Related but different: fz-i89 (a caller trusts only a @spec result that something proved).

Done when: a call whose argument types match exactly one overload gets that overload's result. A test shows `list ++ list` is proper again, and the distiller's numbers fall back by the cost above. The ceilings are lowered to match.
title: A call chooses the @spec overload its argument types match
